title: Client safety & compatibility contract for pagination, retries, and streaming backpressure
creator: Omar Patel
description:
Summary: This PRD defines a forward- and backward-compatible contract for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that covers pagination semantics, retry behavior, streaming APIs (including graceful cancellation and backpressure), and a compatibility/migration path for customers. The goal is to prevent silent behavior divergence between language clients and to enable predictable production guarantees (idempotency, deterministic error surface, and safe automated retries).

Why now: Multiple customers have reported intermittent token loss and opaque cursor errors during large exports. Engineering work to standardize runtime behavior (kernel scheduling, KV cache) requires a clear client contract so that server-side fallbacks and runtime optimizations do not cause client-visible regressions.

Scope: The contract applies to all Redwood-hosted API endpoints that return streaming/iterable results or paginated collections (generation, embeddings, logs, audit exports). It does not rework wire-level protocols (HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1) but defines surface-level semantics that each SDK must implement.

Out-of-scope: deep runtime batching algorithms, transport-level multiplexing changes, and language-specific syntactic sugar beyond the defined surface.

Stakeholders: PM (Marisa Chen), SDK leads (Python: Lina Gomez, TS: Ravi Shah, Go: Henrik Olsen), Serving runtime (Priya Nair), Reliability (Jason Kim), Security (Aisha Rahman).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: SDKs present a uniform streaming type: async iterator (TS/Python) / channel-like consumer (Go) with single cancel() and resume(cursor) methods exposed.

AC-2: Paginated endpoints expose two primitives: `page_token` (opaque string) and `next_page_token`; clients must provide helper helpers to iterate pages and surface deterministic offsets for auditable retries.
AC-3: Standardized error taxonomy - SDKs map service errors into a canonical set: {temporary_retryable, permanent, cursor_expired, quota_exceeded}; mapping table documented in Confluence.

AC-4: Retry behavior: idempotent list/generation calls automatically retry transient network/server errors up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff and jitter; non-idempotent calls require explicit client-provided idempotency token before automatic retry is attempted.

AC-5: Cursor expiry handling: if server returns `410 CURSOR_EXPIRED` with `retry_with_new_cursor` hint, SDKs attempt transparent resume if a checkpoint (last consumed index) exists; otherwise surface a typed CursorExpiredError containing the last confirmed offset and a link to recovery docs.

AC-6: Backpressure contract for streaming: server MAY buffer up to N in-flight tokens; SDKs must provide a configurable high- and low-watermark (default 1024/256 tokens) and expose `pause()`/`resume()` (TS/Python) or `Pause()`/`Resume()` (Go) that apply backpressure to the transport layer. Default implementations must not allocate unbounded memory under spike workloads.

AC-7: Cancellation semantics: calling cancel() MUST close the underlying transport promptly and release resources; SDK must emit a CancellationError and ensure any partial items are either delivered or marked as incomplete with a stable partial-result marker.

AC-8: Cross-language compatibility tests: add nightly integration tests exercising identical scenarios (pagination across >10k items, streaming with induced latency, injected transient errors) and assert parity of outcomes across Python/TS/Go clients.

AC-9: Backwards compatibility: new SDKs must accept older server cursors for at least 12 months; server will return a deprecation header `X-Cursor-Compat: v1->v2` when an older cursor is accepted but will include recommended migration tokens.
AC-10: Documentation: detailed migration guide and deterministic examples for each language (snippet + expected behavior) must be published in Confluence and referenced in SDK CHANGELOGs.
decisions: Decision-2026-03-03: Use a canonical error enum mapping rather than ad-hoc string matching - agreed to reduce client-specific branching.
Decision-2026-03-04: Expose pause()/resume() at the SDK surface instead of relying solely on user-managed backpressure to provide a consistent developer UX.
Decision-2026-03-05: Default retry attempts set to 3 for transient errors; accept explicit opt-out via client config for aggressive low-latency applications.
Decision-2026-03-07: Adopt a 12-month backward-compatibility window for cursor formats and require server-side `X-Cursor-Compat` header for transitional behavior.
Decision-2026-03-09: Security sign-off required because client-side resume tokens contain audit-sensitive offsets; encryption-at-rest and KMS wrapping for stored tokens mandated.
scope_changes: 2026-03-06: Added backpressure high/low watermark requirement after reliability review (previously only suggested).
2026-03-08: Expanded ACs to include explicit Cancellation semantics and partial-result markers following design feedback.
2026-03-09: Security review required flag added after discovery that resume tokens include PII-containing offsets; encryption requirement added to acceptance criteria.
testing_plan: Unit: language-specific unit tests for error mapping, cancellation, and pause/resume behaviors.
Integration: matrix CI that runs Python/TS/Go against a replayable staging harness injecting latency, 500/502/503, and cursor 410 responses.
Chaos: scheduled reliability test that simulates burst traffic and validates memory usage under default backpressure settings.
E2E: migration scenario where a v1 cursor is used against v2 runtime and behavior is asserted for 12-month compatibility window.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Clients may implement inconsistent backpressure leading to memory spikes. Mitigation: provide reference implementations and add runtime telemetry that alerts when in-memory queue grows beyond threshold.

Risk: Automatic retries might cause duplicate side effects for non-idempotent endpoints. Mitigation: require idempotency-token opt-in and document in PRD; add server-side duplicate-suppression header support.
Risk: Cursor tokens may leak corrective offsets containing PII. Mitigation: require server to encrypt cursors and SDKs to treat cursor tokens as secrets; security review and KMS binding required.
